title: Runaway-allocation circuit-breaker and soft-eviction: post-incident action plan
creator: Aisha Ng
description:
Summary: During a dedicated-cluster capacity incident on 2026-03-08 we observed a single tenant produce a sustained allocation surge that exhausted reservation headroom and caused cascading soft evictions across the cluster. Root cause appears to be a combination of reservation mis-sizing for long-tail inference patterns, an aggressive burst top-up policy with no decay guard, and lack of an automatic circuit-breaker to throttle runaway top-ups.

Impact: Multiple customers experienced elevated tail latencies and degraded throughput for 27 minutes. Autoscaler reacted but overshot due to delayed telemetry signals. Billing and token accounting were consistent, but quality of service degraded for higher-tier tenants.

Goal: Implement a defensive, deterministic mitigation suite so future tenant surges are contained locally and cluster-level stability is preserved. The suite includes: a per-tenant allocation circuit-breaker (trip & slow-start), a soft-eviction protocol that preferentially targets the offending workload while preserving KV cache affinity when possible, and a burst token decay policy to limit sustained top-ups.

Notes on trade-offs: Circuit-breaker thresholds must balance false positives for legitimate spikes against speed of mitigation. Soft-eviction must avoid mass cache invalidation; we prefer incremental frame dropping over full KV flush. Burst decay may increase cold-start latency for some workloads but reduces system-wide risk.
action_items: Implement per-tenant allocation circuit-breaker: trips when sustained reservation usage exceeds 70% of max-reserved for >30s, enters slow-start with capped ingress rate — owner: Ethan Morales — due: 2026-03-24

Design and implement soft-eviction policy: evict low-priority or long-running slices first, maintain per-tenant KV cache windows where possible to avoid downstream quality regressions — owner: Priya Kapoor — due: 2026-03-26
Introduce burst-token decay: exponential decay on top-up tokens with configurable half-life per tenant class, default 120s — owner: Miguel Sanchez — due: 2026-03-21
Add telemetry and SLO guard metrics: per-tenant reserve-oversubscription, circuit-breaker trips, soft-eviction counts, KV cache miss delta — owner: Jiyoung Park — due: 2026-03-18
Create automated canary for circuit-breaker: unit/e2e harness that simulates a runaway tenant and verifies containment without collateral eviction — owner: Samir Patel — due: 2026-03-22
Update reservation right-sizing tooling: recommend model-specific profiles using recent 7-day p95 seq length and burst histograms — owner: DataOps Team (contact: Hannah Liu) — due: 2026-03-28
Failover and rollback playbook: document runbook steps for manually overriding circuit-breaker or rebalancing reservations during edge cases — owner: Oncall Lead, Maria Gomez — due: 2026-03-19

Integrate billing signal into topology decisions: ensure topology autoscaler considers billed reservation commitments before speculative node allocation — owner: Backend Infra, Oliver Stein — due: 2026-03-30
Performance test matrix: run scale tests across 100 dedicated tenants with mixed burst profiles, validate tail latency and fairness metrics — owner: QA, Lucas Bennett — due: 2026-03-25
Post-deploy monitoring dashboard and alerting: one-page dashboard and PagerDuty alert for repeated circuit-breaker events within 1h — owner: Observability, Noor Rahman — due: 2026-03-20
